comment: Whole-product and indication-level withdrawals verified from sources opened on 13 November 2026 (Europe/Paris). Only whole-product entries remove a drug from Mainstream. Indication-level entries are reported by the gate and must not silently drop a drug that still has another approved use.

entries.detail: FDA withdrew approval of NDA 215310 for EXKIVITY (mobocertinib succinate) capsule, effective 15 July 2024, after Takeda asked for withdrawal. Takeda announced on 2 October 2023 that it would work with the FDA towards a voluntary withdrawal. The EMA application was withdrawn earlier, on 20 July 2022; that is a different event (the EU marketing application, not a US approval withdrawal).

sources.label: Federal Register 89 FR 57418
sources.detail: Approval is withdrawn as of July 15, 2024. NDA 215310. Published 15 July 2024. Opened 13 November 2026.

sources.label: FDA Withdrawn Cancer Accelerated Approvals
sources.detail: Row for Exkivity (mobocertinib): Accelerated Approval Date 9/15/2021, Withdrawal Date 7/15/2024. Page opened 13 November 2026.

sources.label: Takeda press release
sources.detail: Takeda announced it will be working with the FDA towards a voluntary withdrawal of EXKIVITY in the U.S. Opened 13 November 2026.

sources.label: EMA EPAR Exkivity
sources.detail: EMA application withdrawn on 20 July 2022. This is withdrawal of the EU marketing application, not the US NDA. Opened 13 November 2026.

indication_level_noted.indication: In combination with cetuximab for KRAS G12C mutated locally advanced or metastatic colorectal cancer after fluoropyrimidine-, oxaliplatin-, and irinotecan-based chemotherapy.
indication_level_noted.sure: Listed on the FDA Withdrawn Cancer Accelerated Approvals page opened on 13 November 2026, with Withdrawal Date 9/1/2026. A Federal Register notice for this row was not opened this turn. The NSCLC indication is a different use and is not treated as withdrawn.

indication_level_noted.indication: As monotherapy for locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC after failure of platinum-based and docetaxel chemotherapy (accelerated approval 5/5/2003, withdrawal date 4/25/2012).
indication_level_noted.sure: Listed on the same FDA page. Gefitinib later has a different FDA label use (first-line EGFR exon 19 / L858R) which remains in this snapshot and is not treated as withdrawn.
